title: Urban Region Pre-training and Prompting: A Graph-based Approach

problem.claim: Urban region representation is needed for urban downstream tasks, but acquiring general urban region knowledge and adapting representations to different tasks remains challenging.

gap.claim: Existing methods give limited attention to fine-grained functional layout semantics and to the task-specific features and relationships needed for effective adaptation.

contributions.claim: A graph-based urban region pre-training and prompting framework, GURPP, is proposed for region representation learning.
A subgraph-centric pre-training model constructs an urban region graph and uses contrastive and multi-view learning to pre-train knowledge-rich region embeddings.
Two graph-based prompting methods are designed: a manually defined prompt for explicit task knowledge and a task-learnable prompt for discovering hidden knowledge.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance on various urban region prediction tasks and across different cities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Urban region representation supports various urban downstream tasks.
General knowledge acquisition, transferable fine-grained semantics, and task adaptation remain challenging.
The paper proposes the GURPP framework for urban region representation learning.
GURPP uses an urban region graph and subgraph-centric contrastive and multi-view pre-training to learn transferable embeddings.
Graph-based prompts refine representations for task adaptation, and the authors report superior performance across tasks and cities.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines pre-trained region embeddings with manually defined and task-learnable prompts.

interpretation.claim: Separating transferable representation learning from task-specific prompting may support adaptation across heterogeneous downstream tasks.

application.claim: For urban prediction systems, consider shared graph-based pre-training followed by prompts that encode explicit or learnable task information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which tasks, cities, or data conditions benefit most from either prompting method.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baseline methods, evaluation metrics, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not identify the downstream tasks and cities used in the experiments.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results for the pre-training and prompting components.
